title: Quality and capacity of the host institutions and participating organisations, including hosting arrangements
content:
## 3.2 Quality and capacity of the host institutions and participating organisations, including hosting arrangements

### The host institution: HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont

FIELDWISE is a single-beneficiary MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship. The sole beneficiary, recruiting organisation and academic host is HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (HUN-REN Centre for Agricultural Research, HUN-REN ATK), a public research organisation of the HUN-REN Hungarian Research Network, at Brunszvik u. 2, 2462 Martonvásár, Hungary. Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is recruited into its Agricultural Institute, where the primary supervisor, Dr. Roland Hollós, sits in the Department of Crop Production. The host is chosen for a precise scientific fit: it supplies the modelling and heterogeneous-data-integration environment at the core of the objectives, primary supervision by Dr. Roland Hollós (research associate, Department of Crop Production, and HUN-REN AI Ambassador for the Centre for Agricultural Research; ORCID 0000-0001-5137-7471), access to the wider HUN-REN AI and data-processing infrastructure for computationally intensive analyses, and complementary in-house plant-physiology depth through the Plant Physiology and Metabolomics Department led by Prof. Tibor Janda, whose long experience in drought and abiotic-stress physiology supports the selection and interpretation of physiological validation parameters. The computational and data-processing environment required for multi-source integration and predictive modelling is available in-house, with escalation to the shared HUN-REN research infrastructure where the workload demands it, so no dedicated hardware needs to be provisioned.

HUN-REN ATK is a proven MSCA host. It coordinated and hosted the funded MSCA Individual Fellowship LANDRACES (H2020 grant 752453, MSCA-IF-EF-ST Standard European Fellowship, 2017-2019), evidencing that the beneficiary already possesses the institutional machinery — recruitment, supervision, financial administration and researcher support — that an MSCA-PF requires. Its research standing in the exact methods FIELDWISE relies on is documented: the supervisor's own modelling line (Hollós et al. 2026, on the Biome-BGC model, Geoscientific Model Development) and current Horizon participations verified on CORDIS (COUSIN, AI4SoilHealth, TUdi). Because ATK is a research organisation rather than a university, the fellowship's teaching and outreach exposure is routed deliberately through guest lectures, seminars and practical sessions at MATE and, where institutionally possible, the Agricultural University of Plovdiv, rather than being claimed as an in-house degree-teaching load the host cannot offer.

### Hosting arrangements, integration and support services

The host provides the fellow with a workspace at the Agricultural Institute in Martonvásár, integration into the supervisor's hosting group, administrative and grants support, access to training, and continuation of these arrangements throughout the M25-M30 non-academic placement so that the fellow is not administratively cut adrift during the inter-sectoral phase. Integration into the team is reinforced by the supervision cadence described in Section 3.1 — a weekly one-to-one with the supervisor, a monthly written progress record and quarterly Career Development Plan reviews — which embeds the fellow in the day-to-day scientific life of the Department of Crop Production and, through Prof. Tibor Janda's department, in the institute's physiology environment. Dr. Roland Hollós accepts the primary-supervisor role and carries the modelling-intensive supervision. These hosting arrangements and support services, and the supervisor's formal acceptance, are the beneficiary's own facilities and commitments; they are stated here as the operator's declared position and will be confirmed in ATK's written hosting statement (naming the Part A signatory and the grants-office contact) at grant preparation, rather than presented as already-settled fact.

### The non-academic placement host: AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság

The inter-sectoral mobility element of this European Fellowship is a six-month non-academic placement (M25-M30) at AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság (AGROVIR Kft.), a Hungarian SME founded in 2007 and seated in Budaörs that develops and operates a cloud-based farm-management information system (FMIS). AgroVIR is the operational evaluator: it provides structured requirements consultation from M1 through WP4 and, during the placement, the real farm-management environment in which the DrR web MVP is assessed for usability, data requirements, interoperability and future FMIS integration. Its relevance is commercial rather than academic — it reports no participation in EU-funded research projects, and its stated track record is twenty years of practice in Hungarian commercial agriculture and an FMIS in production use across more than 745,000 hectares in eight countries including Hungary and Bulgaria, the two countries FIELDWISE works in; this track-record framing is the operator's declared position pending the company's written confirmation, and is deliberately not converted into a research claim.

The placement is designed to be robust and low-dependency. It is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings for review, feedback and progress assessment; the fellow does not require direct access to AgroVIR's proprietary software, customer databases, office infrastructure or computing equipment, and AgroVIR supplies only the information and data extracts needed for interoperability testing in protected form (coded or anonymised field identifiers such as 'Field X'). Placement supervision is provided by Miklós Maróti, Managing Director of AgroVIR, whose experience in agricultural digitalisation and farm-management systems anchors the evaluation of the MVP's stress and irrigation outputs within practical workflows, and the fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform. Ownership of placement results follows the grant-agreement default, vesting in HUN-REN ATK as the beneficiary acting through the fellow, with a written placement agreement between the fellow, HUN-REN ATK and AgroVIR to confirm this allocation and the access terms to the fellow's DrR background IP before the placement begins. The placement supervisor and title, the mainly-remote arrangement, the team identification, the person-month commitment and the IP allocation are the placement host's own arrangements and are carried here as the operator's declared position, to be confirmed in AgroVIR's written placement letter; no letter of commitment is submitted for a non-academic placement host, so the placement is evaluated on this Part B argument. What the placement offers that the academic host alone cannot — operational evaluation against a production FMIS, research-to-MVP translation, agricultural-software requirements practice, interoperability assessment and exploitation planning — is the inference that justifies the inter-sectoral move.

### Associated partners linked to the beneficiary

Three associated partners are linked to the beneficiary and add capacity the host does not hold in-house. Full infrastructure, logistics and facilities are detailed in Part B-2 Section 5; the essentials are as follows.

**Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE)** — Faculty of Informatics, Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics, Budapest — supplies the remote-sensing, UAV/hyperspectral and geoinformatics environment and the co-supervisor, Prof. András Jung, who carries the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel harmonisation and scale-transition strand. ELTE's GIS and Remote Sensing Laboratory holds the project's principal spatial instruments: a DJI Matrice 350 RTK industrial drone with Zenmuse L1 (LiDAR/RGB), P1 (45 MP photogrammetry) and H20T (thermal) payloads, an Ultris S5 hyperspectral camera and a Cubert CUVIS laboratory hyperspectral package, together with licensed ArcGIS, ENVI and MATLAB, open geospatial tools (Google Earth Engine, QGIS, SNAP), high-performance computing and secure storage. Practical UAV operations are supported by Dr. Zsófia Varga (flight planning, sensor operation, data acquisition), with the fellow holding an EU A1/A3 pilot licence. The instrument inventory and ELTE's identity are confirmed; ELTE's continuation as an associated partner (rather than beneficiary), the co-supervisor's acceptance, and the written instrument-access arrangement specifying operators, sites, measurement periods and terms are carried as the operator's declared position pending ELTE's written agreement, and Section 3.1 risk R05 provides the constrained-access fallback.

**Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem (MATE)** — Institute of Horticultural Sciences — is the source scientific environment. It provides the heterogeneous 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive that makes processing tomato the development crop, together with tomato plant material, trials, irrigation treatments, agronomic knowledge and the experimental/validation instrument base: TDR and capacitive soil-moisture sensors at 15 and 30 cm, stomatal resistance/conductance equipment, SPAD chlorophyll meters, VIS-NIR (approx. 325-1075 nm) and VIS-NIR-SWIR (approx. 350-2500 nm) leaf spectroradiometers, meteorological monitoring, leaf-temperature and CWSI tools. MATE's project contact is Dr. Sándor Takács, supported by precision-agriculture depth from Prof. Gábor Milics. MATE's identity, instrument base and archive description are confirmed; the contact seat and the rights and data-use conditions governing access to the archive are the operator's declared position, to be documented in MATE's written data-use permission before the action starts (see Section 3.1 risk R10 on commercial-restriction handling).

**КРУМАТИК ЕООД (Krumatic EOOD)** — a Bulgarian technology and digital-solutions company (EIK 201511899, established 2011, Sofia), whose registered manager, sole owner and signatory is Lyubomir Lyubomirov Krumov — provides continuous software-development support from project start: improving the DrR prototype, implementing the validated data/model functions and the crop-configurable architecture, migrating the validated core toward the web MVP, and later Bulgarian farmer-facing dissemination and uptake. Its role is distinct from AgroVIR's: Krumatic builds and disseminates the software vehicle, while AgroVIR evaluates the validated MVP operationally. Its legal identity, contact/signatory and role are confirmed; its SME status and its independence (its prior AgroVIR-platform deployment in Bulgaria stated openly as a commercial-deployment relationship, with no known ownership, employment or family relationship to the fellow or another partner) are the operator's declared position, and the code-IP terms for Krumatic-developed code are a pre-grant development-agreement action rather than a proposal fact.

### Collaborating validation environment and post-fellowship route

The prospective validation in WP3 is carried out at an independent commercial farmer site in Hungary, secured through the fellow's established professional relationship and deliberately kept as a collaborating validation environment rather than a beneficiary or associated partner. Because the site does not currently operate advanced monitoring infrastructure, FIELDWISE installs an automated meteorological station and soil sensors and retains responsibility for all specialised scientific measurements, while the farmer provides the field, routine crop management, agreed irrigation implementation and access for scheduled research activities. This design is the point of the exercise: the site is independent of the historical MATE experiments, so it tests whether learned relationships survive a production environment that was not used to establish them. The written field-access, sensor-installation and treatment-implementation arrangement is the operator's declared position and is obtained through task T3.1 before the campaign; site identity is collected with the arrangement, not fabricated now, and the Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route stands as a contingency-only option subject to formal agreement and scientific suitability. Beyond the fellowship, Институт по зеленчукови култури „Марица“ – Пловдив (the Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute, Bulgarian Agricultural Academy; director Prof. Daniela Ganeva) provides a confirmed post-MSCA replication, local-recalibration and extension route under Bulgarian vegetable-production conditions; it sits on no work-package month line and carries no in-action effort, so it strengthens the exploitation horizon without loading the 24-month scientific plan.

### Global Fellowship provision

FIELDWISE is a European Fellowship arising from an intra-EU move (Bulgaria to Hungary), with the six-month non-academic placement as an extension under CC-07 rather than a Global Fellowship outgoing phase. The Global Fellowship requirement to outline both an outgoing Third Country host and a return host therefore does not apply: there is no Third Country host, and the single academic host throughout is HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont.
